basics.name: Mohammed Barakat
basics.label: Mechanical Engineer | AI & ML Researcher
basics.summary: Mechanical Engineering graduate from the University of Texas at Tyler (GPA 3.9, President's List) with a focus on applying artificial intelligence and machine learning to mechanical engineering problems. Experience in computational modeling, embedded systems, CAD, and AI-driven engineering design.

work.name: University of Texas at Tyler, College of Engineering
work.summary: Applied machine learning techniques to CO₂ sequestration and hydrogen storage research. Used tools including LAMMPS, OVITO, Atomsk, and Wulffpack for nanostructure modeling and simulation.
highlights: Nanostructure modeling using LAMMPS and OVITO
Applied ML to materials science problems

work.name: University of Texas at Tyler, College of Engineering
work.summary: Assisted faculty and students in the engineering lab. Reverse-engineered industrial devices via CAD as part of undergraduate assistant responsibilities.
highlights: Reverse-engineered industrial devices using SolidWorks and Autodesk Inventor
Supported lab operations and student projects

awards.title: President's List
awards.summary: Awarded each semester for achieving a GPA of 4.0 or above.

awards.title: Outstanding Student in College of Engineering
awards.awarder: University of Texas at Tyler, College of Engineering
awards.summary: Nominated for outstanding leadership contributions within the College of Engineering.

publications.name: AI Ethical Practices in Commercial Engineering Organizations
publications.summary: Examines ethical frameworks and best practices for deploying artificial intelligence in commercial mechanical engineering contexts.

projects.name: NICU Sensory Bonding Device
projects.summary: Senior Design capstone project developing a device for NICU patients integrating haptic feedback, scent delivery, and sound with a mobile app interface. Led the software development side of the project.

projects.name: ANN-Integrated Desalination System
projects.summary: Developed an Arduino-based desalination system integrated with an artificial neural network for process optimization.
